messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P1 Private connectivity alert for ACME Corp (pd-8923). Symptoms: elevated packet loss / latency to services in eu-west-2a via PrivateLink. Triggered 2026-03-14T09:12:00Z. Please ack and start troubleshooting.
oncall-amber: Acked. I'm on it. @netops-lee can you confirm whether this looks like a BGP/peering issue or an AZ egress problem?
netops-lee: Looking at edge telemetry now. Initial read: multiple BGP withdraws from peer edge-euw2-az1 between 09:10-09:14 UTC, followed by traffic shifting to az3 egress. Suspect route flap + replication delay causing asymmetric egress -> packet loss.
cust-eng-julia: Customer reports intermittent 502/504 to their backend and repeated reconnections in the last ~10m. They say it started right after a maintenance window on the provider side. Impact: a subset of requests timed out, roughly 3–7% error increase.
edge-bot: Automated alert: bgp_withdraw_rate > threshold on edge-euw2-az1 (09:11:23 -> 09:13:58). DNS anomalies also observed: liveness checks to PrivateLink endpoint resolving to fallback AZ IPs. Link to metrics: https://grafana.internal/graph?panelId=129&from=2026-03-14T09:00&to=2026-03-14T09:20
dev-sam: Can someone paste the BGP neighbor summary from edge-euw2-az1? Need to see AS path churn and whether routes were re-advertised. Use: `sudo /opt/net/tools/bgp-status --neighbor edge-peer-42 --summary`
netops-lee: Pasting trimmed output: ```Neighbor: 10.11.12.42  AS 65012  State: Established  Flaps: 7  LastWithdraw: 09:13:55  RoutesWithdrawn: 120  RoutesAdvertised: 540  AS_PATH changes: yes```
oncall-amber: Good. While @netops-lee digs deeper I'll notify support@acme and spin up temporary traffic-shift to eu-west-1 for critical flows if needed. Julia, can you confirm which endpoints are highest priority?
cust-eng-julia: Priority: api.production.acme.internal and websocket endpoints for realtime. If possible put only these on the fallback path. Non-critical batch jobs can failover later.
netops-lee: Two quick mitigations I can try now: 1) withdraw problematic local next-hop so our routers stop directing traffic to the flapping peer and prefer the stable az3 egress, 2) temporarily adjust route preference to prefer direct peering to partner-edge in az3 for the prefix. I prefer #1 to reduce churn. Will execute in 2m.
oncall-amber: Do it. Add a short maintenance note to status page before change: "Targeted routing change to mitigate packet loss for ACME traffic."
netops-lee: Executing command on controllers: ```for r in $(cat az1-routers); do ssh $r "vtysh -c 'configure terminal' -c 'route-map ACME-PRIORITY deny 10' -c 'exit'"; done``` Applying gracefully.
edge-bot: Config change detected: route-map ACME-PRIORITY applied to az1 egress nodes at 09:18:07 UTC. Monitoring convergence.
dev-sam: Can we also verify DNS TTL and LB health? If endpoints are resolving to az1 IPs, clients may keep using them. What does external resolver TTL look like?
netops-lee: TTL for PrivateLink endpoint was 60s. We pushed a low-TTL health override earlier (to 30s) during maintenance window; that should help but some caches might still hold old records. Retriggering an authoritative refresh now. Command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZXXXXXXXX --change-batch file://refresh.json` (running).
cust-eng-julia: Customer confirms they're still seeing a few 502s but overall error rate dropped to ~1.2% after the route-map change. Very grateful.
oncall-amber: Good. Netops: any sign of the BGP peer recovering or is this persistent flapping?
netops-lee: The peer is still flapping but withdraw rate reduced. Looks like the remote provider is doing microreconfigurations on their side. I opened a support ticket with provider with trace: `ticket#PR-5542` and included the BGP error dumps.
edge-bot: Metric update: total ACME errors fell from 6.8% -> 1.1% over 10m. Latency p50 improved from 210ms -> 120ms.
oncall-amber: Marking P1 mitigated; still open while provider stabilizes. Not moving to resolved until we see 30m stable and provider confirmation.
oncall-amber: @oncall-tina taking Handoff in 20m window. I'll do a formal handoff note: "Applied temporary route-map on az1 to avoid flapping peer; DNS TTL lowered; provider ticket PR-5542 open; customer on fallback for critical endpoints to eu-west-1; monitoring in place."
oncall-tina: Taking handoff. Rechecking alerts and dashboards. Can you drop me the exact commands you ran and the rollback steps?
netops-lee: Commands run: ```# apply route-map for ACME prefixes vtysh -c 'configure terminal' -c 'route-map ACME-PRIORITY deny 10' # invalidate local next-hop to force re-eval vtysh -c 'clear ip route *' # route53 refresh aws route53 change-resource-record-sets .../refresh.json``` Rollback: remove route-map, re-advertise routes, revert TTL. I added the exact snippets to the incident ticket.
oncall-tina: Thanks. I'll continue monitoring for next 30m then update status page. Leaving a note for postmortem: Investigate why local neighbor flapped—possible provider config churn or filter misconfig. Add follow-ups: extend DNS TTL strategy, add per-customer route dampening thresholds.
cust-eng-julia: Thanks everyone — traffic is usable now, but we'll keep our support window open for 2 hours. We'll update if anything else.
oncall-amber: Closing P1 to mitigated state at 09:48 UTC. Will convert to incident for RCA and follow-ups. @netops-lee @dev-sam please coordinate for postmortem.
netops-lee: Will gather BGP dumps, edge logs, and timeline. Posting artifacts to ticket PR-5542 and internal incident doc.
oncall-tina: Handoff complete. If anything regresses, reopen thread with alert. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident state change: P1 -> Mitigated by manual routing change. Incident ID: inc-2026-03-14-ACME-42. Follow-up assigned: netops-lee, dev-sam, cust-eng-julia.
